units.title: Opposites
units.description: Qualities and textures — Common opposite adjectives.

questions.prompt: How do you say "hot" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Hot is "caliente", and its opposite is "frío". For hot weather Spanish says "hace calor" instead.
questions.example: El café está caliente.

questions.prompt: How do you say "rough" (to the touch) in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "áspero" describes a rough surface, like sandpaper, and its opposite is "suave" (smooth).
questions.example: La pared es áspera.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sweet" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Sweet is "dulce". Its opposites are "salado" (salty) and "amargo" (bitter).
questions.example: El jugo es muy dulce.

questions.prompt: How do you say "salty" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Salty is "salado", from "sal" (salt). Its opposite is "dulce" (sweet).
questions.example: La sopa está salada.

questions.prompt: How do you say "hard" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "duro" means hard as in firm, not soft (the opposite of "blando"); hard meaning difficult is "difícil".
questions.example: El pan está duro.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: El café está muy caliente.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "El café está muy caliente.", meaning the coffee is very hot; the other choices change the quality word to salty, sweet or empty.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "La sopa está muy salada" means the soup is very salty; "salada" ends in -a because it describes the feminine word "sopa".

questions.prompt: Say that the bread is hard.
acceptableAnswers: El pan está duro.
El pan es duro.
El pan está muy duro.
El pan está duro ahora.
Está duro el pan.
El pan está bien duro.
El pan está muy duro ahora.
El pan está algo duro.
questions.explanation: "El pan está duro." says the bread is hard (firm); "duro" is the opposite of "blando", and "está" describes its current state.

questions.prompt: How do you say "soft" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "blando" means soft as in not hard, like a pillow or a ripe fruit, and it is the opposite of "duro".
questions.example: La cama es blanda.

questions.prompt: How do you say "clean" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "limpio" means "clean"; its opposite in this lesson is "sucio" (dirty).
questions.example: Mi cuarto está limpio.

questions.prompt: How do you say "dirty" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Dirty is "sucio". Its opposite is "limpio" (clean), so don't mix up the pair.
questions.example: Mi carro está sucio.

questions.prompt: How do you say "full" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Full is "lleno", and its opposite is "vacío" (empty).
questions.example: El vaso está lleno.

questions.prompt: How do you say "empty" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Empty is "vacío", with an accent on the í. Its opposite is "lleno" (full).
questions.example: El vaso está vacío.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: La mesa está muy limpia.
questions.explanation: The sentence "La mesa está muy limpia." means the table is very clean; "sucia" (dirty), "llena" (full) and "dura" (hard) sound different.

questions.prompt: Say that the glass is empty.
acceptableAnswers: El vaso está vacío.
El vaso está vacío ahora.
Está vacío el vaso.
El vaso está completamente vacío.
El vaso está totalmente vacío.
El vaso ya está vacío.
questions.explanation: "El vaso está vacío." uses "vacío" (empty), the opposite of "lleno", with "estar" because it describes a current state.

questions.prompt: How do you say "open" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Open is "abierto", and its opposite is "cerrado" (closed).
questions.example: El mercado está abierto.

questions.prompt: How do you say "closed" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: Closed is "cerrado", and its opposite is "abierto" (open).
questions.example: El banco está cerrado hoy.

questions.prompt: How do you say "wet" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Wet is "mojado", and its opposite is "seco" (dry).
questions.example: El piso está mojado.

questions.prompt: How do you say "dry" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "seco" means dry, as in "La ropa está seca"; its opposite is "mojado" (wet).
questions.example: La toalla está seca.

questions.prompt: How do you say "heavy" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "pesado" means heavy; its opposite is "ligero" (light). "fuerte" means strong, not heavy.
questions.example: Mi mochila está pesada.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: La ropa está seca
questions.explanation: The sentence "La ropa está seca" means the clothes are dry; the other choices change the last word to dirty, new or cold.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "La caja está llena" means the box is full, using "llena", the opposite of "vacía" (empty).

questions.prompt: Say that the clothes are wet.
acceptableAnswers: La ropa está mojada.
Mi ropa está mojada.
Las prendas están mojadas.
La ropa está mojada ahora.
Está mojada la ropa.
Las prendas de vestir están mojadas.
La ropa está muy mojada.
La ropa está empapada.
Mi ropa está muy mojada.
questions.explanation: "La ropa está mojada." uses "mojada" (wet), which agrees with the feminine noun "ropa"; the opposite is "seca" (dry).

questions.prompt: How do you say "light (weight)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ligero" means light in weight, the opposite of "pesado" (heavy); in much of Latin America "liviano" is also very common.
questions.example: Mi bolsa es ligera.

questions.prompt: How do you say "strong" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "fuerte" means strong, the opposite of "débil" (weak).
questions.example: Mi papá es fuerte.

questions.prompt: How do you say "weak" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "débil" means weak and is the opposite of "fuerte" (strong); it has the same form for masculine and feminine.
questions.example: Estoy débil por la gripe.

questions.prompt: How do you say "loud" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "ruidoso" means loud or noisy, the opposite of "silencioso" (quiet).
questions.example: El carro es ruidoso.

questions.prompt: How do you say "quiet" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "silencioso" means quiet (making no noise) and is the opposite of "ruidoso" (noisy).
questions.example: El salón está silencioso.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: La caja está muy pesada
questions.explanation: "La caja está muy pesada" means the box is very heavy; the wrong choices change the last word to sucia (dirty), cerrada (closed) or mojada (wet).

questions.prompt: Say that the room is very quiet.
acceptableAnswers: El cuarto está muy silencioso
La habitación está muy silenciosa
El cuarto es muy silencioso
La habitación es muy silenciosa
El cuarto está muy tranquilo
La habitación está muy tranquila
El cuarto es muy tranquilo
La habitación es muy tranquila
El cuarto está muy callado
La habitación está muy callada
La recámara está muy silenciosa
La recámara está muy tranquila
questions.explanation: "El cuarto está muy silencioso" uses silencioso for quiet, the opposite of ruidoso, and agrees with a masculine noun.

units.title: Emotions
units.description: How do you feel? — Common emotion words.

questions.prompt: How do you say "happy (content)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "contento" means happy or pleased and is used with estar: "Estoy contento".
questions.example: Estoy contento con mi trabajo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "grateful" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "agradecido" means grateful and comes from the verb agradecer (to thank).
questions.example: Estoy muy agradecido contigo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "angry" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "enojado" means angry and is the usual word in Latin America: "Estoy enojado".
questions.example: Mi papá está enojado.

questions.prompt: How do you say "scared" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "asustado" means scared and comes from susto (a fright): "Estoy asustado".
questions.example: El niño está asustado.

questions.prompt: How do you say "surprised" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "sorprendido" means surprised and looks like the English word: "Estoy sorprendido".
questions.example: Estoy sorprendido con el regalo.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Hoy estoy muy contento con mi familia.
choices: Hoy estoy muy enojado con mi familia.
Hoy estoy muy cansado con mi familia.
Hoy estoy muy asustado con mi familia.
Hoy estoy muy contento con mi familia.
questions.answer: Hoy estoy muy contento con mi familia.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Hoy estoy muy contento con mi familia.", meaning they are very happy today with their family. The other options swap in different feeling words that sound clearly different.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Estoy muy enojado hoy." means "I am very angry today." You use estar with enojado because anger is a feeling that changes, and muy makes it stronger.

questions.prompt: Say that you are scared tonight.
acceptableAnswers: Estoy asustado esta noche.
Esta noche estoy asustado.
Estoy muy asustado esta noche.
Estoy asustada esta noche.
Esta noche estoy asustada.
Tengo miedo esta noche.
Esta noche tengo miedo.
Esta noche estoy muy asustada.
Estoy muy asustada esta noche.
Esta noche estoy muy asustado.
Me siento asustado esta noche.
Me siento asustada esta noche.
questions.explanation: "Estoy asustado esta noche." uses estar plus asustado to say you feel scared, and esta noche means tonight.

questions.prompt: How do you say "bored" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "aburrido" means bored with estar ("Estoy aburrido"), but boring with ser ("Es aburrido").
questions.example: Estoy aburrido en casa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "excited" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "emocionado" means excited, as in "Estoy emocionado por el viaje"; it does not mean emotional in a sad way.
questions.example: Estoy emocionado por el viaje.

questions.prompt: How do you say "nervous" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Nervous" is "nervioso" (nerviosa for a woman); "tranquilo" means calm, "enojado" angry and "celoso" jealous.
questions.example: Estoy nervioso por el examen.

questions.prompt: How do you say "calm" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "tranquilo" means calm and is the opposite of "nervioso" or "preocupado" (worried).
questions.example: Mi hermano está tranquilo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in love" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "enamorado" means "in love", as in "Estoy enamorado". "contento" means happy, "aburrido" means bored and "preocupado" means worried.
questions.example: Mi amigo está enamorado.

questions.prompt: Which sentence did you hear?
questions.audioText: Hoy estoy muy tranquilo y contento.
choices: Hoy estoy muy tranquilo y contento.
Hoy estoy muy tranquilo y enojado.
Hoy estoy muy aburrido y contento.
Hoy estoy muy nervioso y contento.
questions.answer: Hoy estoy muy tranquilo y contento.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Hoy estoy muy tranquilo y contento." meaning they feel very calm and happy today; the other choices change one feeling word.

questions.prompt: Say that you are worried today.
acceptableAnswers: Hoy estoy preocupado.
Estoy preocupado hoy.
Hoy estoy preocupada.
Estoy preocupada hoy.
Hoy estoy muy preocupado.
Hoy estoy muy preocupada.
Hoy me siento preocupado.
Hoy me siento preocupada.
Estoy muy preocupado hoy.
Estoy muy preocupada hoy.
Me siento preocupado hoy.
Me siento preocupada hoy.
questions.explanation: "Hoy estoy preocupado." uses estar for a feeling, with "preocupado" meaning worried ("preocupada" if the speaker is a woman).

questions.prompt: How do you say "tired" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cansado" means "tired", as in "Estoy cansado". "emocionado" means excited, "orgulloso" means proud and "enojado" means angry.
questions.example: Estoy cansado después del trabajo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "worried" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "preocupado" means "worried", as in "Estoy preocupado". "nervioso" is nervous, which is close but not the same feeling.
questions.example: Mi mamá está preocupada.

questions.prompt: How do you say "proud" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "orgulloso" means "proud", as in "Estoy orgulloso de ti". "celoso" means jealous and "enojado" means angry.
questions.example: Estoy orgulloso de mi hijo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "jealous" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "celoso" means "jealous", as in "Él está celoso". "asustado" means scared and "orgulloso" means proud.
questions.example: Mi amigo está celoso.

questions.prompt: How do you say "confused" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "confundido" means "confused" and looks like the English word. "contento" means happy, "aburrido" means bored and "cansado" means tired.
questions.example: Estoy confundido con la tarea.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Hoy estoy muy cansado
questions.explanation: The sentence is "Hoy estoy muy cansado", meaning "Today I am very tired". The other choices swap in different feelings: happy, nervous and angry.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Estoy muy orgulloso de ti" means "I am very proud of you"; use "estoy" with a feeling and "de" before the person you are proud of.

questions.prompt: Say that you are bored.
acceptableAnswers: Estoy aburrido.
Estoy aburrida.
Me siento aburrido.
Me siento aburrida.
Estoy muy aburrido.
Estoy muy aburrida.
Yo estoy aburrido.
Yo estoy aburrida.
questions.explanation: "Estoy aburrido." uses estar plus an emotion word to say how you feel right now. Use "aburrida" if the speaker is a woman.

units.title: Question Words
units.description: Asking questions — The core interrogative words.

questions.prompt: How do you say "what" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "qué" means "what" and takes an accent in questions, as in "¿Qué es?". "quién" means who.
questions.example: ¿Qué quieres comer?

questions.prompt: How do you say "who" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "quién" means "who" and takes an accent in questions, as in "¿Quién es?". "dónde" means where and "cuándo" means when.
questions.example: ¿Quién es ella?

questions.prompt: How do you say "when" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cuándo" asks about time (when), and it takes a written accent because it is a question word.
questions.example: ¿Cuándo llega tu hermano?

questions.prompt: How do you say "where" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "dónde" asks about place (where), as in "¿Dónde está el baño?".
questions.example: ¿Dónde está el baño?

questions.prompt: How do you say "why" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "por qué" means why and is written as two words with an accent; "porque", one word with no accent, means because.
questions.example: ¿Por qué estás triste?

questions.prompt: Which sentence did you hear?
questions.audioText: ¿Dónde está la casa?
questions.explanation: The speaker asks "¿Dónde está la casa?", which means "Where is the house?". The other choices change the question word or the noun, so they ask something different.

questions.prompt: Ask a friend (informal 'you') where he or she is from, using the question word for 'where'.
acceptableAnswers: ¿De dónde eres?
¿De dónde eres tú?
¿Tú de dónde eres?
¿Tú eres de dónde?
¿De dónde tú eres?
questions.explanation: "¿De dónde eres?" combines "de" (from) with the question word "dónde" (where), which keeps its accent, and "eres", the informal tú form of "ser".

questions.prompt: How do you say "how" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cómo" asks about manner or way (how), as in "¿Cómo estás?"; "qué" means what.
questions.example: ¿Cómo estás?

questions.prompt: How do you say "which" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cuál" means which (one) and is used to choose among options; "quién" asks who and "de quién" asks whose.
questions.example: ¿Cuál es tu libro?

questions.prompt: How do you say "how much" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cuánto" means "how much" and asks about an amount, as in "¿Cuánto cuesta?"; the plural "cuántos" means "how many".
questions.example: ¿Cuánto cuesta el libro?

questions.prompt: How do you say "how many" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cuántos" is the plural form, used to count things, so it means "how many", as in "¿Cuántos libros tienes?"
questions.example: ¿Cuántos años tienes?

questions.prompt: How do you say "whose" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: Spanish has no single word for "whose"; it says "de quién" (literally "of whom"), as in "¿De quién es este libro?"
questions.example: ¿De quién es este libro?

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: ¿Cuántos amigos tienes aquí?
questions.explanation: The speaker asks "¿Cuántos amigos tienes aquí?", using cuántos (how many) with the plural noun amigos; the other choices change one word you can hear.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "¿Cuántos libros tienes?" asks how many books someone has. Cuántos is the plural form of cuánto, used when you count things.

questions.prompt: Ask someone how many brothers or sisters they have.
acceptableAnswers: ¿Cuántos hermanos tienes?
¿Cuántos hermanos tiene usted?
¿Cuántos hermanos tienen ustedes?
¿Cuántos hermanos y hermanas tienes?
¿Cuántos hermanos y hermanas tiene usted?
¿Cuántos hermanos tienes tú?
¿Cuántos hermanos o hermanas tienes?
¿Cuántos hermanos o hermanas tiene usted?
¿Tú cuántos hermanos tienes?
¿Cuántos hermanos tiene?
¿Cuántos hermanos y hermanas tienen ustedes?
questions.explanation: "¿Cuántos hermanos tienes?" uses "cuántos" because you are counting a plural noun, and "tienes" is the informal tú form of "tener".

units.title: Telling Time
units.description: What time is it? — Basic time-telling expressions.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué hora ___?
questions.explanation: Spanish asks the time with "es": ¿Qué hora es? The question uses the verb ser, not hay, tener or estar.
questions.example: ¿Qué hora es?

questions.prompt: Es la ___ (one o'clock).
questions.explanation: One o'clock is singular and "la" is feminine because it agrees with "hora", so the number must be "una", not uno. Only one o'clock uses "Es"; other hours use "Son las".
questions.example: Es la una de la tarde.

questions.prompt: Son las ___ (two o'clock).
questions.explanation: From two o'clock on, Spanish uses plural "Son las" plus the number, so two o'clock is "dos". "Una" would need "Es la".

questions.prompt: Son las tres y ___ (half).
questions.explanation: Half past is "y media", with the feminine "media" agreeing with the understood word "hora". "Medio" is masculine and "mitad" is not used for telling time.

questions.prompt: Son las cuatro y ___ (quarter).
questions.explanation: A quarter past is "y cuarto", using the masculine noun "cuarto" (a fourth of an hour). "Cuarta" is not used in this expression.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Son las cinco y media.
questions.explanation: "Son las cinco y media." means it is half past five; the other choices change the hour or the minutes, which sound clearly different.

questions.prompt: Say that it is half past five.
acceptableAnswers: Son las cinco y media.
Son las cinco y treinta.
Son las cinco y media de la tarde.
Son las cinco y media de la mañana.
Son las 5:30.
Son las 5:30 de la tarde.
Son las cinco treinta.
Son las cinco y treinta de la tarde.
Son las cinco y treinta de la mañana.
Son las 5:30 de la mañana.
questions.explanation: Half past is "y media", and hours from two to twelve take plural "Son las", so you say "Son las cinco y media." "Y treinta" is also correct.

questions.prompt: Es ___ (midnight).
questions.explanation: Midnight is "medianoche" (literally half-night), as in "Es medianoche". "Mediodía" means noon, while "tarde" and "mañana" are parts of the day.

questions.prompt: Es ___ (noon).
questions.explanation: Noon is "mediodía" (literally half-day), as in "Es mediodía". "Medianoche" is midnight, and "mañana" and "tarde" are parts of the day.

questions.prompt: Son las cinco en ___ (exactly).
questions.explanation: "punto" completes "en punto", the fixed phrase for exactly on the hour, as the clue says.
questions.example: Son las cinco en punto.

questions.prompt: Son las seis menos ___ (quarter).
questions.explanation: "cuarto" is a quarter: "las seis menos cuarto" is a quarter to six, and "cuarto" is masculine, so "cuarta" does not fit.
questions.example: Son las seis menos cuarto.

questions.prompt: Llego a las siete de la ___ (morning).
questions.explanation: "mañana" completes "de la mañana", which means in the morning (a.m.), as the clue says: "llego a las siete de la mañana".

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Son las ocho y media.
questions.explanation: The sentence "Son las ocho y media." means it is half past eight; "y media" adds thirty minutes to the hour.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Son las tres y media de la tarde
questions.explanation: "Son las tres y media de la tarde" means it is half past three in the afternoon. You use "y media" for half past, and "de la tarde" for the afternoon hours.

questions.prompt: Say that it is a quarter past four.
acceptableAnswers: Son las cuatro y cuarto.
Son las cuatro y quince.
Son las cuatro y cuarto de la tarde.
Son las cuatro y cuarto de la mañana.
Son las 4:15.
Son las cuatro y quince de la tarde.
Son las cuatro quince.
Son las 4:15 de la tarde.
Son las cuatro y quince de la mañana.
Son las 4:15 de la mañana.
questions.explanation: "Son las cuatro y cuarto." uses "y cuarto" to add a quarter hour after four, and the verb is plural "son" because the hour is "las cuatro".

questions.prompt: Ceno a las nueve de la ___ (night).
questions.explanation: "noche" completes "de la noche", which means at night (p.m.), as the clue says: "ceno a las nueve de la noche".

questions.prompt: Trabajo por la ___ (afternoon).
questions.explanation: The English clue says "afternoon", and "tarde" is the Spanish word for it; "por la tarde" means 'in the afternoon'.

questions.prompt: Son las ocho y ___ (ten minutes).
questions.explanation: The clue says ten minutes, and "diez" is ten, so the time is 'las ocho y diez' (8:10).

questions.prompt: Llega a las once y ___ (twenty).
questions.explanation: The clue says twenty minutes, and "veinte" is twenty, so the time is 'las once y veinte' (11:20).

questions.prompt: El tren sale a la una y ___ (five).
questions.explanation: The clue says five minutes, and "cinco" is five, so the train leaves at 'la una y cinco' (1:05).

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Salgo a las seis de la mañana.
choices: Salgo a las seis de la tarde.
Salgo a las siete de la mañana.
Salgo a las seis de la mañana.
Salgo a las seis de la noche.
questions.answer: Salgo a las seis de la mañana.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Salgo a las seis de la mañana.", meaning 'I leave at six in the morning'; the hour and the part of the day both matter.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Son las tres y diez" means 'It is ten past three' (3:10); say the hour first, then y and the minutes.

questions.prompt: Say that the train arrives at one in the afternoon.
acceptableAnswers: El tren llega a la una de la tarde.
El tren llega a la una por la tarde.
El tren llega a la 1:00 de la tarde.
El tren llega a la una p. m.
A la una de la tarde llega el tren.
El tren llega a la 1 de la tarde.
El tren llega a la 1:00 p. m.
El tren llega a las 13:00.
questions.explanation: "El tren llega a la una de la tarde." uses "a la una" (singular, because one o'clock is only one hour) for 'at one', and "de la tarde" for 'in the afternoon'.

units.title: Basic Prepositions
units.description: Where is it? — Common location prepositions.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "en" means "in", as in "El gato está en la caja"; the other options mean around, near and next to.
questions.example: El libro está en la mesa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "on" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "sobre" means "on" (on top of a surface), as in "El libro está sobre la mesa"; Spanish also often uses "en" for this. The other options mean around, next to and far from.
questions.example: El libro está sobre la mesa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "under" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "debajo de" means "under", as in "debajo de la mesa". "encima de" and "sobre" mean the opposite, on top of.
questions.example: El gato está debajo de la mesa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "next to" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "al lado de" means "next to" (right beside), as in "al lado de la puerta". "cerca de" only means near.
questions.example: Mi casa está al lado de la escuela.

questions.prompt: How do you say "between" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "entre" means "between", as in "entre la casa y el parque". "al lado de" means next to and "dentro de" means inside.
questions.example: El banco está entre la tienda y el parque.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: El libro está debajo de la silla.
choices: El libro está encima de la silla.
El libro está cerca de la silla.
El libro está lejos de la silla.
El libro está debajo de la silla.
questions.answer: El libro está debajo de la silla.
questions.explanation: "El libro está debajo de la silla." means the book is under the chair; the other sentences use different place words (on top of, far from, near).

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: El libro está al lado de la puerta
questions.explanation: "El libro está al lado de la puerta" uses "al lado de" to say the book is right next to the door.

questions.prompt: Say that the cat is between the house and the park.
acceptableAnswers: El gato está entre la casa y el parque.
El gato está entre el parque y la casa.
El gato se encuentra entre la casa y el parque.
El gato se encuentra entre el parque y la casa.
questions.explanation: "El gato está entre la casa y el parque." uses "entre" for between two places; the order of the two places can be swapped.

questions.prompt: How do you say "in front of" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "delante de" means "in front of", as in "delante de la casa"; in Latin America you will also hear "enfrente de". "dentro de" means inside.
questions.example: El carro está delante de mi casa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "behind" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "detrás de" means behind, at the back of something: "El gato está detrás de la puerta." Don't confuse it with "debajo de" (under).
questions.example: El perro está detrás de la puerta.

questions.prompt: How do you say "near (to)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cerca de" means near (to): "La tienda está cerca de mi casa." Its opposite is "lejos de" (far from).
questions.example: Mi casa está cerca de la escuela.

questions.prompt: How do you say "far from" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "lejos de" means far from: "El aeropuerto está lejos de la ciudad." Its opposite is "cerca de" (near).
questions.example: Mi trabajo está lejos de mi casa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "inside" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "dentro de" means inside, in the interior of something: "Las llaves están dentro de la caja." Its opposite is "fuera de" (outside).
questions.example: El gato está dentro de la casa.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: El perro está debajo de la mesa.
choices: El perro está cerca de la mesa.
El perro está debajo de la mesa.
El perro está encima de la mesa.
El perro está detrás de la mesa.
questions.answer: El perro está debajo de la mesa.
questions.explanation: "El perro está debajo de la mesa." means the dog is under the table; "debajo de" means under, while the other choices change that one word.

questions.prompt: Say that the keys are inside the box.
acceptableAnswers: Las llaves están dentro de la caja.

Las llaves están en el interior de la caja.
questions.explanation: "Las llaves están dentro de la caja." uses "dentro de" for inside; "en" can also work as a simpler way to say in.

questions.prompt: How do you say "outside" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "fuera de" means outside (of): "El perro está fuera de la casa." Its opposite is "dentro de" (inside).
questions.example: El perro está fuera de la casa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "above" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "encima de" means "above" or "on top of", as in "La lámpara está encima de la mesa"; "debajo de" is its opposite, below.
questions.example: El libro está encima de la mesa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "around" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "alrededor de" means around, on every side of something: "Hay árboles alrededor de la casa."
questions.example: Hay árboles alrededor de la casa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "through" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "a través de" means through, from one side to the other: "Caminamos a través del parque."
questions.example: Veo el parque a través de la ventana.

questions.prompt: How do you say "against" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "contra" means against, touching or pushing on something: "La bicicleta está contra la pared." Unlike "delante de" and "fuera de", it takes no "de".
questions.example: La bicicleta está contra la pared.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: El gato está debajo de la silla.
choices: El gato está detrás de la silla.
El gato está cerca de la silla.
El gato está debajo de la silla.
El gato está encima de la silla.
questions.answer: El gato está debajo de la silla.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "El gato está debajo de la silla.", meaning the cat is under the chair; "debajo de" means below or under.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: El libro está encima de la mesa
questions.explanation: "El libro está encima de la mesa" means the book is on top of the table; "encima de" is followed by the thing it sits above.

questions.prompt: Say that the book is under the table.

El libro está por debajo de la mesa.
questions.explanation: "El libro está debajo de la mesa." uses "debajo de" for below or under, followed by the thing it is under; "abajo de" is a common Latin American variant.

units.title: Nature & Outdoors
units.description: The world outside — Basic nature vocabulary.

questions.prompt: How do you say "coral reef" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "arrecife de coral" is the Spanish for "coral reef" ("arrecife" means reef); playa, roca and flor mean beach, rock and flower.
questions.example: Quiero ver un arrecife de coral.

questions.prompt: How do you say "moon" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "luna" means moon. It is feminine: "la luna", as in "La luna está llena."
questions.example: La luna está hermosa hoy.

questions.prompt: How do you say "star" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "estrella" means "star", as in "Hay muchas estrellas en el cielo"; flor and lago mean flower and lake.
questions.example: Veo una estrella en el cielo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sky" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cielo" means sky. It is masculine: "el cielo", as in "El cielo está azul."
questions.example: El cielo está azul.

questions.prompt: How do you say "tree" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "árbol" means tree. It is masculine and has a written accent on the a: "el árbol".
questions.example: Hay un árbol en mi jardín.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: El lago está cerca de la playa.
choices: El cielo está cerca de la playa.
El lago está lejos de la playa.
El lago está cerca de la roca.
El lago está cerca de la playa.
questions.answer: El lago está cerca de la playa.
questions.explanation: The sentence "El lago está cerca de la playa." means the lake is near the beach; the other choices change one word (roca, cielo, lejos).

questions.prompt: Say that the sky is blue.
acceptableAnswers: El cielo es azul.
El cielo está azul.
El cielo es de color azul.
El cielo se ve azul.
questions.explanation: "El cielo es azul." states the sky's color; "cielo" is masculine, so it takes "el" and "azul" does not change.

questions.prompt: How do you say "flower" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "flor" means flower. It is feminine: "la flor", and its plural is "flores".
questions.example: Esta flor es muy hermosa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "grass" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "hierba" means grass (la hierba). In much of Latin America people also say "pasto" for the grass in a lawn or field.
questions.example: Los caballos comen hierba.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sea" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "mar" means sea (el mar). "Arena" is the sand on the beach and "cielo" is the sky above it.
questions.example: Me gusta nadar en el mar.

questions.prompt: How do you say "sand" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "arena" means sand (la arena), as in la arena de la playa. "Isla" means island, not sand.
questions.example: La arena está caliente.

questions.prompt: How do you say "rock" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "roca" means rock (la roca), a big piece of stone. "Flor" is a flower and "luna" is the moon.
questions.example: Hay una roca grande aquí.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: La luna está en el cielo.
choices: La flor está en el cielo.
La luna está en el mar.
La luna está en la roca.
La luna está en el cielo.
questions.answer: La luna está en el cielo.
questions.explanation: You hear "La luna está en el cielo.", which means the moon is in the sky. Listen for "luna" (moon) and "cielo" (sky), the two words that change in the other choices.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: La flor está en la hierba
questions.explanation: "La flor está en la hierba" means the flower is in the grass. Use "está" to say where something is, and remember that "flor" and "hierba" are both feminine, so they take "la".

questions.prompt: Say that the sea is big.
acceptableAnswers: El mar es grande.
El mar es muy grande.

El mar es enorme.
Grande es el mar.
El mar es inmenso.
El mar es bien grande.
questions.explanation: "El mar es grande." uses "es" to describe what the sea is like; "grande" has the same form for masculine and feminine nouns, so it does not change after "el mar".

questions.prompt: How do you say "lake" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "lago" means lake (el lago), a body of fresh water surrounded by land. "Isla" is an island, which is land surrounded by water.
questions.example: El lago es muy hermoso.

questions.prompt: How do you say "island" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "isla" means "island", land with water all around it; lago is a lake and arrecife de coral is a coral reef.
questions.example: Vivo en una isla pequeña.

questions.prompt: How do you say "leaf" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "hoja" means leaf (la hoja de un árbol); the h is silent. "Hierba" is grass, not a leaf.
questions.example: Esta hoja es verde.

questions.prompt: How do you say "mountain" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "montaña" means mountain (la montaña); note the ñ. "Lago" is a lake.
questions.example: La montaña es muy alta.

questions.prompt: How do you say "beach" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "playa" means beach (la playa). "Mar" is the sea next to it, not the beach itself.
questions.example: Voy a la playa el domingo.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: El lago es muy grande.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "El lago es muy grande.", describing a big lake; the other choices change one word (bonito, mar, isla) that sounds clearly different.

questions.prompt: Say that the leaf is green.
acceptableAnswers: La hoja es verde.
La hoja está verde.
La hoja es muy verde.
Es verde la hoja.
La hoja es de color verde.
La hoja es bien verde.
Verde es la hoja.
questions.explanation: "La hoja es verde." uses the feminine article "la" because "hoja" (leaf) is feminine, and "verde" has the same form for masculine and feminine nouns.

units.title: Fruits & Vegetables
units.description: At the market — Common fruits and vegetables.

questions.prompt: How do you say "apple" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "manzana" means apple (la manzana). "Sandía" is a watermelon and "coco" is a coconut.

questions.prompt: How do you say "banana" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "plátano" is a common word for "banana", for example in Mexico; in some countries it means plantain, and you may also hear "banano" or "guineo".
questions.example: Quiero un plátano, por favor.

questions.prompt: How do you say "orange (fruit)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "naranja" means orange, the fruit (la naranja); it is also the word for the color orange. "Pera" is a pear.
questions.example: Quiero jugo de naranja.

questions.prompt: How do you say "strawberry" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "fresa" means "strawberry"; in Chile and Argentina people also say "frutilla".
questions.example: Me gusta la fresa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "grape" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "uva" means grape (la uva); a bunch of grapes is un racimo de uvas. "Limón" is a lemon or lime.
questions.example: Quiero una uva.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Quiero una manzana, por favor.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Quiero una manzana, por favor.", asking politely for an apple at the market. The other choices name different fruits.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Me gustan las uvas y las fresas
questions.explanation: "Me gustan las uvas y las fresas" means "I like grapes and strawberries"; gustan is plural because the fruits are plural.

Yo quisiera una banana.
questions.explanation: "Quiero un plátano." uses quiero (I want) with un, because plátano is masculine; in many countries you will also hear "una banana" or "un banano".

questions.prompt: How do you say "watermelon" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "sandía" means watermelon (la sandía); note the accent on the í. "Papa" is a potato.
questions.example: La sandía es dulce.

questions.prompt: How do you say "pineapple" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "piña" is the Spanish word for pineapple, the tropical fruit with spiky leaves; note the ñ, which sounds like the 'ny' in 'canyon'.

questions.prompt: How do you say "pear" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "pera" means "pear"; cebolla is an onion, calabaza is a squash and piña is a pineapple.
questions.example: Quiero una pera.

questions.prompt: How do you say "cherry" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cereza" means "cherry"; sandía is a watermelon, pepino is a cucumber and kiwi is a kiwi.
questions.example: La cereza es roja.

questions.prompt: How do you say "lemon" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "limón" means "lemon"; note the accent on the o, and don't confuse it with lechuga (lettuce).

questions.prompt: What did you hear?

questions.prompt: Say that you want a watermelon, politely, as you would at the market.

questions.prompt: How do you say "peach" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "durazno" is the Latin American word for "peach"; in Spain people say "melocotón".

questions.prompt: How do you say "mango" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: mango → mango. Common fruits and vegetables.

questions.explanation: "coco" is the Spanish word for coconut; don't confuse it with "aguacate" (avocado) or "zanahoria" (carrot).

questions.prompt: How do you say "kiwi" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: kiwi → kiwi. Common fruits and vegetables.

questions.prompt: How do you say "tomato" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "tomate" means "tomato" and looks almost like the English word; "papa" is a potato, "maíz" is corn and "uva" is a grape.

questions.prompt: How do you say "potato" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "papa" is the Latin American word for "potato"; in Spain people say "patata".

questions.prompt: How do you say "carrot" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "zanahoria" means "carrot"; coco is a coconut, pepino is a cucumber and naranja is an orange.

questions.prompt: How do you say "onion" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "cebolla" is the Spanish word for onion; watch the double l, which sounds like the y in 'yes' in most of Latin America.

questions.prompt: How do you say "garlic" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "ajo" is the Spanish word for garlic; the j sounds like a strong English h.

questions.prompt: How do you say "lettuce" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "lechuga" means lettuce, the green leafy vegetable used in salads, as in "una ensalada de lechuga".

questions.prompt: How do you say "cucumber" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "pepino" means cucumber, the long green vegetable often sliced into salads.

questions.prompt: How do you say "pepper (vegetable)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "pimiento" is the bell pepper (the vegetable, not the spice); you may also hear "morrón" or "pimentón" in some countries, and "chile" for hot peppers.
questions.example: Quiero un pimiento rojo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "corn" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "maíz" is the general word for corn; corn on the cob is often called "elote" in Mexico and "choclo" in South America.
questions.example: Me gusta el maíz.

questions.prompt: How do you say "avocado" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "aguacate" means avocado and is used in Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean; in much of South America people say "palta".
questions.example: Quiero un aguacate, por favor.

questions.prompt: How do you say "pumpkin" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "calabaza" means pumpkin or squash; in Argentina and Uruguay you will also hear "zapallo".

Quiero una calabaza grande, por favor.

units.title: Kitchen Verbs
units.description: Cooking actions — Present-tense "yo" conjugation of common cooking verbs.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (cortar) las verduras.
questions.explanation: The subject "yo" (I) takes the present-tense ending -o, so cortar becomes "corto"; -as, -an and -amos belong to tú, ellos and nosotros.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (mezclar) los ingredientes.
questions.explanation: With "yo" (I), -ar verbs end in -o, so mezclar becomes "mezclo"; the other forms match él, nosotros or ellos.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (hervir) el agua.
questions.explanation: Hervir changes its stem e to ie in the yo form and takes -o, giving "hiervo"; "hervimos" (we) keeps the plain stem but doesn't match "yo".

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (freír) el pescado.
questions.explanation: Freír takes -o with "yo" and keeps a written accent on the í, giving "frío"; "fríe", "fríes" and "fríen" are for él, tú and ellos.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (hornear) un pastel.
questions.explanation: The subject "yo" (I) takes -o on -ar verbs, so hornear becomes "horneo"; "horneas", "hornean" and "horneamos" fit tú, ellos and nosotros.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Ellos cortan las verduras en la cocina.
choices: Ellos cortan las verduras en la cocina.
Ellos mezclan las verduras en la cocina.
Ellos cortan los pasteles en la cocina.
Ellos cortan las verduras en la mesa.
questions.answer: Ellos cortan las verduras en la cocina.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Ellos cortan las verduras en la cocina." which means they cut the vegetables in the kitchen; the other choices change one word you can hear: mesa, mezclan or pasteles.

questions.prompt: Say that you are frying the fish.
acceptableAnswers: Yo frío el pescado.
Frío el pescado.
Estoy friendo el pescado.
Yo estoy friendo el pescado.
questions.explanation: With "yo" the verb freír becomes "Yo frío el pescado." and keeps the written accent on the í; the subject pronoun can be dropped in Spanish.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (lavar) los platos.
questions.explanation: With "yo" (I), -ar verbs end in -o, so lavar becomes "lavo"; the other options match nosotros, ellos or él.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (verter) la leche.
questions.explanation: Verter changes e to ie in the yo form and ends in -o, giving "vierto"; "vertemos" keeps the plain stem and belongs to nosotros.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (añadir) sal a la sopa.
questions.explanation: The subject "yo" (I) takes -o on -ir verbs, so añadir becomes "añado"; "añade", "añades" and "añaden" match él, tú and ellos.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (calentar) la comida.
questions.explanation: With "yo" the present-tense ending is -o, and calentar changes its stem e to ie in this form, giving "caliento". Only "calentamos" keeps the plain stem, and that form is for "nosotros".
questions.meaning: I heat up, I warm up

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (servir) la cena.
questions.explanation: The subject "yo" takes the ending -o, and servir changes its stem e to i, so the form is "sirvo". The other options end in -e, -es or -en, which belong to él, tú or ellos.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Yo caliento la sopa
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Yo caliento la sopa", meaning "I heat the soup"; the other choices change the verb or the noun to a clearly different word.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Yo sirvo la sopa." means "I serve the soup." With yo, servir ends in -o and its stem changes from e to i.

questions.prompt: Say that you pour the milk.
acceptableAnswers: Yo vierto la leche
Vierto la leche
Estoy vertiendo la leche.
Yo estoy vertiendo la leche.
Echo la leche.
Yo echo la leche.
Sirvo la leche.
Yo sirvo la leche.
Estoy echando la leche.
Estoy sirviendo la leche.
questions.explanation: "Yo vierto la leche" means "I pour the milk"; verter changes e to ie and ends in -o with yo, and the subject yo can be dropped.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (probar) la salsa.
questions.explanation: After "yo" the verb ends in -o, and probar changes its stem o to ue, giving "pruebo". "Pruebas", "prueba" and "prueban" are the tú, él and ellos forms.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (pelar) las papas.
questions.explanation: Pelar is a regular -ar verb, so "yo" takes the ending -o and the form is "pelo". The endings -a, -as and -amos go with él, tú and nosotros.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (picar) la cebolla.
questions.explanation: Picar is a regular -ar verb, so "yo" takes the ending -o, giving "pico". "Pican", "pica" and "picamos" match ellos, él and nosotros.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (batir) los huevos.
questions.explanation: Batir is an -ir verb, and the "yo" form drops -ir and adds -o, giving "bato". The options "bates", "baten" and "batimos" are for tú, ellos and nosotros.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (asar) el pollo.
questions.explanation: Asar is a regular -ar verb, so the "yo" form ends in -o: "aso". The forms with -a, -an and -as belong to él, ellos and tú.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Yo pelo las papas y pico la cebolla.
choices: Yo pelo las papas y pico la cebolla.
Yo pelo las papas y aso la cebolla.
Yo pelo las papas y pico el ajo.
Yo pelo las papas y pruebo la cebolla.
questions.answer: Yo pelo las papas y pico la cebolla.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Yo pelo las papas y pico la cebolla." This means they peel the potatoes and chop the onion, with both verbs in the yo form ending in -o.

questions.prompt: Say that you are cooking the chicken in the oven (roasting it).
acceptableAnswers: Yo aso el pollo.
Aso el pollo.
Estoy asando el pollo.
Yo estoy asando el pollo.
Estoy asando el pollo al horno.
Aso el pollo en el horno.
Yo aso el pollo en el horno.
Estoy horneando el pollo.
Yo horneo el pollo.
Horneo el pollo.
Yo estoy horneando el pollo.
Estoy asando el pollo en el horno.
questions.explanation: Asar means to roast, and the yo form ends in -o, so "Yo aso el pollo." is the natural way to say it. Spanish often drops "yo", so "Aso el pollo." works too.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (colar) la pasta.
questions.explanation: With "yo" the ending is -o, and colar changes its stem o to ue, so the form is "cuelo". "Colamos" keeps the plain stem because it is the nosotros form.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (rallar) el queso.
questions.explanation: Rallar is a regular -ar verb, so "yo" takes the ending -o, giving "rallo". "Rallan", "rallamos" and "ralla" are the ellos, nosotros and él forms.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (exprimir) un limón.
questions.explanation: Exprimir is a regular -ir verb, and the "yo" form ends in -o: "exprimo". The endings -es, -en and -imos go with tú, ellos and nosotros.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (revolver) el arroz.
questions.explanation: The subject "yo" takes the ending -o, and revolver changes its stem o to ue, giving "revuelvo". The other options end in -e, -en or -es, which match él, ellos and tú.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (tapar) la olla.
questions.explanation: Tapar is a regular -ar verb, so the "yo" form ends in -o: "tapo". The forms with -a, -amos and -as are for él, nosotros and tú.
questions.meaning: I cover, I put the lid on

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Yo pelo las papas y las cebollas.
choices: Yo lavo las papas y las cebollas.
Yo pelo las papas y las cebollas.
Yo pelo las papas y los tomates.
Yo pico las papas y las cebollas.
questions.answer: Yo pelo las papas y las cebollas.
questions.explanation: The sentence is "Yo pelo las papas y las cebollas." and means 'I peel the potatoes and the onions.' The other choices change one word: pico (chop), tomates (tomatoes) or lavo (wash).

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: Yo corto el pan con un cuchillo
questions.explanation: The phrase "Yo corto el pan con un cuchillo" means 'I cut the bread with a knife.' Cortar is a regular -ar verb, so the yo form ends in -o.

questions.prompt: Say that you are cooking the soup.
acceptableAnswers: Yo cocino la sopa.
Cocino la sopa.
Estoy cocinando la sopa.
Yo estoy cocinando la sopa.
Yo cocino una sopa.
Estoy preparando la sopa.
Yo preparo la sopa.
Cocino una sopa.
Hago la sopa.
Yo hago la sopa.
Estoy haciendo la sopa.
questions.explanation: Cocinar is a regular -ar verb, so with yo it ends in -o: "Yo cocino la sopa." You can also drop "yo" because the ending already shows who is cooking.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (encender) la estufa.
questions.explanation: The subject "yo" takes the "-o" ending, and encender changes e to ie in the stem, so it is "enciendo". "Enciende", "enciendes" and "encendemos" match other subjects.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (apagar) el horno.
questions.explanation: With "yo", a regular -ar verb like apagar ends in -o, giving "apago". "Apaga", "apagan" and "apagamos" go with él, ellos and nosotros.
questions.meaning: I turn off, I switch off

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (medir) la harina.
questions.explanation: Medir changes e to i in the stem and takes the "-o" ending for "yo", so it is "mido". "Mides", "miden" and "medimos" belong to tú, ellos and nosotros.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (untar) mantequilla en el pan.
questions.explanation: Untar is a regular -ar verb, so "yo" takes the "-o" ending: "unto". "Unta", "untas" and "untan" are for él, tú and ellos.
questions.example: Unto mantequilla en el pan.

questions.prompt: Yo ___ (enfriar) el postre.
questions.explanation: Enfriar takes a written accent in the "yo" form, "enfrío", to keep the í stressed. "Enfría" and "enfrías" are for él and tú, and "enfriamos" for nosotros.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Yo enciendo la estufa para el desayuno.
choices: Yo enciendo la estufa para el almuerzo.
Yo enciendo el horno para el desayuno.
Yo apago la estufa para el desayuno.
Yo enciendo la estufa para el desayuno.
questions.answer: Yo enciendo la estufa para el desayuno.
questions.explanation: The sentence you hear is "Yo enciendo la estufa para el desayuno." It means I turn on the stove for breakfast; the other choices change one word, such as apago (turn off) or almuerzo (lunch).

questions.prompt: Say that you turn off the oven.
acceptableAnswers: Yo apago el horno.
Apago el horno.
Estoy apagando el horno.
Yo estoy apagando el horno.
questions.explanation: With "yo", apagar ends in -o, so the answer is "Yo apago el horno." The subject yo can also be dropped in Spanish, as in "Apago el horno."

units.title: Quantifiers
units.description: How much, how many — Common quantity words.

questions.prompt: How do you say "more" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "más" means more, as in "quiero más agua"; it needs the accent, because "mas" without it is a rare word meaning 'but'.
questions.example: Quiero más agua, por favor.

questions.prompt: How do you say "less" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "menos" means less, as in "más o menos"; "poco" means a little, not less.
questions.example: Quiero menos azúcar, por favor.

questions.prompt: How do you say "a lot" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "mucho" means a lot, as in "Me gusta mucho."
questions.example: Tengo mucho trabajo hoy.

questions.prompt: How do you say "little (not much)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "poco" means little or not much, as in "tengo poco dinero" (I have little money).
questions.example: Tengo poco tiempo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "several" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "varios" means several and agrees with the noun, as in "varios libros" or "varias casas".
questions.example: Tengo varios amigos aquí.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Tengo muchos amigos en la ciudad.
choices: Tengo pocos amigos en la ciudad.
Tengo muchos amigos en la casa.
Tengo muchos amigos en la ciudad.
Tengo muchos libros en la ciudad.
questions.answer: Tengo muchos amigos en la ciudad.
questions.explanation: The sentence "Tengo muchos amigos en la ciudad." means 'I have many friends in the city'; "muchos" means many, while "pocos" means few.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: The phrase "Quiero más agua, por favor" means 'I want more water, please'; "más" means more.

questions.prompt: Say that you have little money.
acceptableAnswers: Tengo poco dinero.
Yo tengo poco dinero.
Tengo muy poco dinero.
Tengo poca plata.
Tengo muy poca plata.
Yo tengo poca plata.
questions.explanation: "Tengo poco dinero." uses "poco" for 'little (not much)' before a noun that cannot be counted, so it stays in the singular.

questions.prompt: How do you say "enough" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "suficiente" means enough, as in "Tengo suficiente dinero."
questions.example: Tengo suficiente comida.

questions.prompt: How do you say "too much" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "demasiado" means too much, as in "Hay demasiado ruido"; "pocos" means few.
questions.example: Hay demasiado ruido aquí.

questions.prompt: How do you say "each" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cada" means each and never changes form, as in "cada día" (each day) or "cada persona".
questions.example: Estudio español cada día.

questions.prompt: How do you say "none" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "ninguno" means none or not one, as in "No hay ninguno."
questions.example: Ninguno de mis amigos vive aquí.

questions.prompt: How do you say "half" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "mitad" is the noun for half, as in "la mitad de la pizza"; "cuarto" is a quarter and "parte" is just a part.
questions.example: Quiero la mitad del pastel.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Tengo suficiente dinero para el café.
choices: Tengo demasiado dinero para el café.
Tengo suficiente dinero para el té.
Tengo suficiente dinero para el café.
Tengo suficiente tiempo para el café.
questions.answer: Tengo suficiente dinero para el café.
questions.explanation: The sentence heard was "Tengo suficiente dinero para el café.", meaning I have enough money for the coffee; the other choices change one word (tiempo, té, demasiado).

questions.prompt: Say that you have enough money.
acceptableAnswers: Tengo suficiente dinero.
Yo tengo suficiente dinero.
Tengo dinero suficiente.
Tengo bastante dinero.
Tengo suficiente plata.
Yo tengo bastante dinero.
Yo tengo suficiente plata.
Tengo bastante plata.
Tengo plata suficiente.
questions.explanation: "Tengo suficiente dinero." uses "suficiente" (enough) before the noun, and you can drop the subject "yo" because "tengo" already shows who is speaking.

questions.prompt: How do you say "some" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "algunos" means "some" before a plural masculine noun, as in "algunos amigos"; with feminine nouns it becomes "algunas".
questions.example: Algunos niños juegan en el parque.

questions.prompt: How do you say "many" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "muchos" means "many" before a plural masculine noun, as in "muchos libros"; with feminine nouns it becomes "muchas".
questions.example: Tengo muchos libros en casa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "few" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "pocos" means "few" before a plural masculine noun, as in "pocos días"; it is the opposite of "muchos".
questions.example: Hay pocos estudiantes hoy.

questions.prompt: How do you say "most" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "mayoría" means "majority", and "most" is said as "la mayoría de", as in "la mayoría de los estudiantes".
questions.example: La mayoría de mis amigos estudia español.

questions.prompt: How do you say "only" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "solo" means "only" when it modifies a word, as in "Solo tengo un hermano"; it is written without an accent.
questions.example: Solo quiero agua, gracias.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Tengo pocos amigos aquí.
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Tengo pocos amigos aquí.", meaning 'I have few friends here'; "pocos" is the word for 'few'.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Tengo muchos libros en casa" means 'I have many books at home'; "muchos" goes before a plural masculine noun.

questions.prompt: Say that you only have one brother.
acceptableAnswers: Solo tengo un hermano.
Tengo solo un hermano.
Tengo un hermano solamente.
Tengo un solo hermano.
Yo solo tengo un hermano.
Solamente tengo un hermano.
Yo tengo solo un hermano.
Yo solamente tengo un hermano.
Tengo solamente un hermano.
Yo tengo un solo hermano.
Tengo únicamente un hermano.
questions.explanation: "Solo tengo un hermano." uses "solo" to mean 'only' right before the verb it modifies.

questions.prompt: How do you say "almost" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "casi" means almost and goes before the word it softens, as in "casi todo" (almost everything). "Solo" means only and "cada" means each.
questions.example: Casi son las cinco.

questions.prompt: How do you say "nothing" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "nada" means nothing. After a verb, Spanish also keeps "no", as in "No quiero nada" (I don't want anything).
questions.example: No tengo nada en la bolsa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "double" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "doble" means double (twice as much) and has the same form for masculine and feminine, as in "un café doble". "Extra" only means additional.
questions.example: Quiero un café doble, por favor.

questions.prompt: How do you say "three times as much" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "triple" means "three times as much", just as "doble" means "twice as much", as in "el triple de trabajo".
questions.example: Quiero una porción triple.

questions.prompt: How do you say "only (the one and only)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "único" means "the only one" or "single", as in "Es mi único hermano" (He is my only brother).
questions.example: Eres mi único amigo aquí.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: No quiero más café, gracias.
questions.explanation: The sentence "No quiero más café, gracias." means "I don't want more coffee, thanks." The word "más" (more) sounds different from "mucho", "ese" and "otro".

questions.prompt: Say that you want nothing.
acceptableAnswers: No quiero nada.
Yo no quiero nada.
No quiero nada, gracias.
Yo no quiero nada, gracias.
No quiero nada de nada.
No deseo nada.
Yo no deseo nada.
questions.explanation: "No quiero nada." means "I don't want anything." Spanish keeps "no" before the verb and then adds "nada" after it.

questions.prompt: How do you say "additional (more than usual)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "extra" means "additional" and does not change for gender, as in "una hora extra".
questions.example: Necesito una silla extra.

questions.prompt: How do you say "entire" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "entero" means "entire" or "whole" and agrees with its noun, as in "Comí la pizza entera".
questions.example: Me comí el pastel entero.

questions.prompt: How do you say "partial" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "parcial" means "partial", the opposite of "entero" (whole), as in "un pago parcial".
questions.example: Es un pago parcial.

questions.prompt: How do you say "approximately" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "aproximadamente" means "approximately", as in "aproximadamente diez personas"; in speech, "más o menos" is also common.
questions.example: Tengo aproximadamente veinte libros.

questions.prompt: How do you say "exactly" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "exactamente" means "exactly", the opposite of "aproximadamente", as in "Son exactamente las tres".
questions.example: Son exactamente las cinco.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Tengo pocos libros en casa.
questions.explanation: Listen for "pocos", which means "few" and ends in -os because it agrees with the plural masculine noun: "Tengo pocos libros en casa." means "I have few books at home." The word "muchos" would mean "many", the opposite.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: The phrase "Quiero comer la pizza entera" means "I want to eat the whole pizza"; "entera" agrees with the feminine noun "pizza".

questions.prompt: Say that there are exactly ten people here.
acceptableAnswers: Hay exactamente diez personas aquí.
Aquí hay exactamente diez personas.
Hay diez personas aquí exactamente.
Hay exactamente diez personas.
Aquí hay diez personas exactamente.
Hay justo diez personas aquí.
Hay exactamente diez personas acá.
Acá hay exactamente diez personas.
Aquí hay justo diez personas.
Hay diez personas exactamente aquí.
questions.explanation: Use "hay" for "there are" and "exactamente" for "exactly", placed before the number: "Hay exactamente diez personas aquí." Unlike "aproximadamente" (approximately), "exactamente" says the amount is precise.

units.title: Basic Conversation Phrases
units.description: Everyday small talk — Common small-talk and reaction phrases.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Make yourself at home" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Siéntete como en casa" literally means 'feel as if at home'. It uses the friendly tú command, so say it to a friend or family guest.
questions.example: Pasa, siéntete como en casa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "How's it going?" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¿Qué tal?" is the short, friendly way to ask how things are going. Note the opening ¿ and the accent on "qué" in a question.
questions.example: Hola Luis, ¿qué tal?

questions.prompt: How do you say "Long time no see" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Cuánto tiempo sin verte" literally means 'how much time without seeing you'. "Verte" is the tú form, so use it with friends.
questions.example: Hola Ana, cuánto tiempo sin verte.

questions.prompt: How do you say "See you later" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Hasta luego" literally means 'until later'. It is the everyday goodbye when you expect to see someone again.
questions.example: Hasta luego, nos vemos mañana.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Take care" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Cuídate" is the friendly tú command of cuidarse (to look after yourself), and people say it when parting from someone. The other options mean "congratulations", "I don't know" and "I agree".
questions.example: Adiós, cuídate mucho.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Hasta luego, nos vemos mañana.
questions.explanation: "Hasta luego, nos vemos mañana." means 'See you later, we'll see each other tomorrow.' The wrong choices end in ahora, hoy and pronto, which sound different from mañana.

questions.prompt: Tell a friend to relax and not worry about it.
acceptableAnswers: Tómalo con calma
Tranquilo
Tranquila
No te preocupes
Tranquilo, no te preocupes
Tranquila, no te preocupes
Relájate
Relájate, no te preocupes
Tranquilízate
Relájate y no te preocupes
Cálmate, no te preocupes
No te preocupes por eso
questions.explanation: "Tómalo con calma" literally means 'take it calmly' and is a friendly tú command. People use it to tell someone to relax.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Have a good day" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Que tengas un buen día" is the set phrase for wishing a friend a good day, so learn it as one chunk. The other options ask someone to repeat, ask how things are, and say "make yourself at home".
questions.example: Adiós, que tengas un buen día.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Welcome back" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Bienvenido de vuelta" greets someone who has returned. Say "bienvenida" to a woman, and note that "bienvenido de nuevo" is also common.
questions.example: Bienvenido de vuelta, Pablo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "I don't understand" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "No entiendo" is the yo form of "entender" (the e changes to ie) with "no" in front. No subject is needed because the ending already shows 'I'.
questions.example: Perdón, no entiendo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Can you repeat that?" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "¿Puedes repetirlo?" literally asks "Can you repeat it?" with the verb repetir. "Habla despacio, por favor" asks someone to speak slowly, not to repeat.
questions.example: Perdón, ¿puedes repetirlo?

questions.prompt: How do you say "Speak slowly, please" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Habla despacio, por favor" uses "despacio" (slowly), while "más alto" would mean louder. This is the tú command; to a stranger, say "Hable despacio, por favor".
questions.example: No entiendo, habla despacio, por favor.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: ¿Puedes hablar más despacio, por favor?
questions.explanation: You hear "¿Puedes hablar más despacio, por favor?", which politely asks someone to speak more slowly. Listen for the one word that changes in the other choices: louder ("alto"), eat ("comer"), or "otra vez" instead of "por favor".

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "¡Cuánto tiempo sin verte!" means 'Long time no see!' and is a friendly set phrase you say to someone you haven't seen for a long time.

questions.prompt: Tell a friend you do not understand, and ask them to say it again.
acceptableAnswers: No entiendo. ¿Puedes repetirlo?
No entiendo, ¿puedes repetirlo, por favor?
No entiendo. ¿Puedes repetir, por favor?
No entiendo. ¿Me lo puedes repetir?
No entiendo. ¿Puedes repetir eso?
No entiendo. ¿Me lo repites, por favor?
No entiendo. ¿Lo puedes repetir?
No entiendo. ¿Puedes decirlo otra vez?
No entiendo. ¿Puedes repetirme eso?
questions.explanation: "No entiendo. ¿Puedes repetirlo?" joins "No entiendo" (I don't understand) with "¿Puedes repetirlo?" (Can you repeat it?), a polite way to ask a friend to say something again.

questions.prompt: How do you say "What does that mean?" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "¿Qué significa eso?" uses "significar" (to mean) and "eso" (that). "Qué" takes an accent because it is a question word.
questions.example: Perdón, ¿qué significa eso?

questions.prompt: How do you say "I don't know" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "No sé" comes from "saber" (to know). "Sé" needs the accent to mean 'I know' and not the pronoun "se".
questions.example: No sé dónde está.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Of course" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Claro" (literally "clear") is the everyday way to say "of course" when agreeing to something. The other options mean "I don't know", "likewise" and "take care".
questions.example: Claro, con mucho gusto.

questions.prompt: How do you say "No problem" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "No hay problema" literally means 'there is no problem', using "hay" (there is). It is the usual friendly reply to thanks or a request.
questions.example: Gracias, no hay problema.

questions.prompt: How do you say "That's okay" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Está bien" means "it's fine" and is used to accept an apology or agree to something. The other options mean "congratulations", "I don't understand" and "see you later".
questions.example: No te preocupes, está bien.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: No entiendo, ¿puedes repetirlo?
questions.explanation: The speaker says "No entiendo, ¿puedes repetirlo?", which means 'I don't understand, can you repeat it?'. The wrong choices change one word that sounds clearly different.

questions.prompt: Tell someone it's fine and that there is no problem.
acceptableAnswers: Está bien, no hay problema.
No hay problema, está bien.
Claro, no hay problema.
Está bien, no hay ningún problema.
Todo bien, no hay problema.
No hay problema, todo está bien.
No hay ningún problema, está bien.
Tranquilo, no hay problema.
Todo está bien, no hay problema.
questions.explanation: "Está bien, no hay problema." combines "Está bien" (it's fine) with "No hay problema" (no problem), two friendly everyday replies.

questions.prompt: How do you say "I agree" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Estoy de acuerdo" literally means "I am in agreement": Spanish uses estar + de acuerdo where English uses the verb "agree".
questions.example: Estoy de acuerdo contigo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "I disagree" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "No estoy de acuerdo" is the negative of "Estoy de acuerdo": put "no" before the verb to say you disagree.
questions.example: Lo siento, no estoy de acuerdo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Good luck" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Buena suerte" means "good luck"; suerte is feminine, so the adjective is buena, not bueno.
questions.example: Mañana es tu examen, buena suerte.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Congratulations" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Felicidades" is what you say for a birthday, a new job or any good news; in much of Latin America you will also hear Felicitaciones.
questions.example: Felicidades por tu nuevo trabajo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "I'm sorry" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Perdón" is a quick apology for a small mistake, like bumping into someone. For deeper regret, "lo siento" is also used.
questions.example: Perdón, fue mi culpa.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Estoy muy contento hoy
questions.explanation: "Estoy muy contento hoy" means "I am very happy today"; contento is the word for happy or glad, and estar is used for how you feel.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Buena suerte, hasta luego" means "Good luck, see you later"; it combines two phrases from this unit that you can say when saying goodbye.

questions.prompt: Tell a friend that the plan is fine with you and you accept it.
acceptableAnswers: Está bien para mí.
Para mí está bien.
Me parece bien.
Me parece bien el plan.
Para mí el plan está bien.
El plan está bien para mí.
Está bien, lo acepto.
Estoy de acuerdo con el plan.
Acepto el plan.
Me parece bien, lo acepto.
Me parece bien el plan, lo acepto.
Está bien, acepto el plan.
questions.explanation: "Está bien para mí." uses está bien (it's fine) plus para mí (for me) to say the plan works for you; "Me parece bien" is a common alternative.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Excuse me (getting attention)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Disculpe" is the polite usted form you use to get a stranger's attention, such as a waiter or someone on the street.
questions.example: Disculpe, ¿dónde está el baño?

questions.prompt: How do you say "It's a pleasure" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Es un placer" means "it's a pleasure"; you can say it when you meet someone or after you help them.
questions.example: Es un placer conocerla, señora.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Same to you" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Igualmente" means "likewise" and is the usual reply when someone wishes you something, like ¡Buen fin de semana!
questions.example: Gracias, igualmente.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Take it easy" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "Tómalo con calma" literally means "take it calmly". It is the friendly tú way to tell someone to relax or not stress.
questions.example: No te preocupes, tómalo con calma.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Good job" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "Buen trabajo" means "good job"; trabajo is masculine, and bueno shortens to buen before a masculine noun.
questions.example: Buen trabajo, Ana.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Disculpe, ¿dónde está el baño?
questions.explanation: The speaker says "Disculpe, ¿dónde está el baño?", using the polite usted way to get attention and ask where the bathroom is.

questions.prompt: Tell someone it's a pleasure to meet them.
acceptableAnswers: Es un placer.
Es un placer conocerte.
Es un placer conocerlo.
Es un placer conocerla.
Mucho gusto.
Encantado.
Encantada.
Es un placer conocerlos.
Es un placer conocerlas.
Un placer.
Encantado de conocerte.
Encantada de conocerte.
questions.explanation: "Es un placer." means 'It's a pleasure' and is said when you meet someone. Add "conocerte" for someone you call tú, "conocerlo/conocerla" for usted, or "conocerlos/conocerlas" for a group; "Mucho gusto" and "Encantado/Encantada" also work.

units.title: Colors & Shapes
units.description: More colors, and basic shapes — Additional colors and basic geometric shapes.

questions.prompt: How do you say "pink" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "rosa" means pink; in much of Latin America you will also hear rosado.
questions.example: Mi vestido es rosa.

questions.prompt: How do you say "purple" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "morado" is purple; "dorado" is gold, "naranja" is orange and "gris" is grey.
questions.example: Me gusta el color morado.

questions.prompt: How do you say "gray" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "gris" means gray and keeps the same form for masculine and feminine nouns: un gato gris, una casa gris.
questions.example: El gato es gris.

questions.prompt: How do you say "brown" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "marrón" means brown; in much of Latin America "café" is also very common for brown.
questions.example: Mis zapatos son marrón.

questions.prompt: How do you say "turquoise" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "turquesa" is turquoise, the blue-green color; "dorado" is gold and "plateado" is silver.
questions.example: El mar es turquesa.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: El gato es gris.
questions.explanation: The sentence "El gato es gris." says the cat is gray; the other choices change the color or adjective to a clearly different word.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.answer: La casa es de color morado
questions.explanation: "La casa es de color morado" means "The house is purple." Use "es de color" plus a color word to say what color something is, and notice that "morado" matches the masculine word "color."

questions.prompt: Say that the car is brown.
acceptableAnswers: El carro es marrón.
El coche es marrón.
El carro es café.
El auto es marrón.
El auto es café.
El carro es de color marrón.
El carro es de color café.
El coche es café.
El auto es de color marrón.
El coche es de color marrón.
El coche es de color café.
El auto es de color café.
questions.explanation: "El carro es marrón." uses marrón for brown; carro and coche both mean car, and café is a common alternative for brown in Latin America.

questions.prompt: How do you say "gold" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "dorado" means gold, the color; "azul marino" is navy blue and "rosa" is pink.
questions.example: El anillo es dorado.

questions.prompt: How do you say "silver" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "plateado" means silver; it comes from plata, the metal silver. With feminine nouns it changes to plateada (una llave plateada).
questions.example: Mi celular es plateado.

questions.prompt: How do you say "beige" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: beige → beige. Additional colors and basic geometric shapes.
questions.example: Mi sofá es beige.

questions.prompt: How do you say "navy blue" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "azul marino" is navy blue, literally 'marine blue', while azul claro is light blue. It does not change form: pantalones azul marino.
questions.example: Mi chaqueta es azul marino.

questions.prompt: How do you say "circle" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "círculo" means circle; it carries an accent on the first i because the stress falls on the third-to-last syllable.
questions.example: Dibujo un círculo.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: Mi casa tiene una puerta dorada.
choices: Mi mesa tiene una puerta dorada.
Mi casa tiene una puerta grande.
Mi casa tiene una puerta dorada.
Mi casa tiene una ventana dorada.
questions.answer: Mi casa tiene una puerta dorada.
questions.explanation: The speaker said "Mi casa tiene una puerta dorada.", meaning 'My house has a gold door'; dorada is feminine to match puerta.

questions.prompt: Say that the star is silver.
acceptableAnswers: La estrella es plateada.
La estrella es de color plateado.
Es una estrella plateada.
La estrella es de color plata.
Es una estrella de color plateado.
La estrella es color plata.
La estrella es color plateado.
La estrella es de plata.
Es una estrella color plata.
questions.explanation: "La estrella es plateada." uses plateada in the feminine form because estrella is a feminine noun.

questions.prompt: How do you say "square" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "cuadrado" means square; it also works as an adjective, as in una mesa cuadrada.
questions.example: La mesa es un cuadrado.

questions.prompt: How do you say "triangle" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "triángulo" is the three-sided shape (tri- means three, as in English). Note the accent on the first a.
questions.example: Dibujo un triángulo rojo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "rectangle" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "rectángulo" is the four-sided shape with two long and two short sides; "cuadrado" is a square, with all sides equal.
questions.example: La puerta es un rectángulo.

questions.prompt: How do you say "star (shape)" in Spanish? ___
questions.explanation: "estrella" means star, both the shape and the one in the sky; it is feminine: una estrella.
questions.example: Dibujo una estrella amarilla.

questions.prompt: How do you say "heart (shape)" in Spanish?
questions.explanation: "corazón" means heart, both the organ and the shape. It has an accent on the last o.
questions.example: Dibujo un corazón rojo.

questions.prompt: What did you hear?
questions.audioText: La mesa es un rectángulo.
questions.explanation: The sentence "La mesa es un rectángulo." says the table is a rectangle; the other choices name different shapes that sound clearly different.

questions.prompt: Say this aloud:
questions.explanation: "Una estrella y un corazón" means a star and a heart; remember estrella is feminine (una) and corazón is masculine (un).

questions.prompt: Say that the table is square.
acceptableAnswers: La mesa es cuadrada.
Es una mesa cuadrada.
La mesa tiene forma cuadrada.
La mesa es de forma cuadrada.
Es cuadrada la mesa.
La mesa es cuadrada, no redonda.
La mesa tiene forma de cuadrado.
